title: SCIM provisioning: idempotency tokens, orphaned-account reconciliation, and safe deprovisioning
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Improve SCIM provisioning robustness and correctness across hosted and Dedicated customers by adding idempotency at the request layer, a reconciliation job to fix orphaned accounts/groups after partial failures, and safer deprovisioning semantics that integrate with audit logging and admin controls. This ticket covers design, implementation, rollout with feature flags, observability, and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria:
- SCIM POST/PUT requests are processed idempotently when clients provide an idempotency token or when externalId is present.
- Deprovisioning events (DELETE) are soft-tombstoned first, with configurable delay and audit event emission.
- Reconciliation job can detect and recover orphaned users/groups caused by partial failures within 24 hours and emits audit records for changes made.
- Retry/backoff policy implemented with jitter and circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures during provider outages.
- Console exposes a per-tenant "SCIM resync" button and shows last successful sync time.
- End-to-end integration tests added and passing in CI for common failure scenarios.
implementation_notes: Key design choices: 1) Introduce an idempotency token header (X-SCIM-Idempotency) accepted by Redwood; when present, operations are deduplicated in the provisioning service using a write-once token store with TTL. 2) Use externalId as a secondary dedupe key where provided by IdP. 3) On delete we mark user/group with tombstone metadata: tombstone=true, tombstone_expires_at=timestamp; background workers will remove fully after configurable grace period. 4) Reconciliation job scans tenant change logs, compares SCIM directory state with internal account state, and schedules corrective actions rather than applying immediate destructive changes. 5) All SCIM operations must emit structured audit events (scim.operation_id, scim.op_type, actor, tenant, resource_ids) to the audit log pipeline. 6) Provide admin console controls to trigger manual resync and to preview reconciliation plan before applying. 7) Feature-flag rollout by tenant: scim-idempotency and scim-safe-deprovision.
data_migration_plan: Add a new idempotency_tokens table (tenant_id, token, op_hash, created_at, result_ref) with a TTL of 7 days by default. Backfill is not required; tokens are created on new requests. Add tombstone columns to users and groups tables and backfill with tombstone=false for existing rows. Reconciliation job will run in dry-run mode for 48h before enabling corrective writes for the first set of tenants.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token dedupe logic and tombstone semantics.
- Integration tests simulating: duplicate POSTs, network partition during provisioning, provider returning 5xx mid-flow, group rename collisions, and delete followed by create races.
- End-to-end scenario: connect a test IdP (Okta) using SCIM, run bulk user import, simulate intermittent failures and verify reconciliation recovers intended state.
- Load test: ensure idempotency store scales to 1000 req/s per region without contention.
- Security test: ensure tombstoned users cannot authenticate or be used for session creation.
monitoring_and_observability: Dashboards and alerts to add: 1) SCIM request success/failure rate by tenant and op_type. 2) Idempotency token dedupe rate and token store latency. 3) Reconciliation job success/failure rate and items processed per run. 4) Tombstone growth graph and tombstone expiry backlog. 5) Audit ingestion lag for SCIM events. Alerts: high failure rate (>5% p95) for >15m, reconciliation job crash loop, tombstone backlog > 1000 unexplained tombstones. Logs should include scim.operation_id and tenant_id for traceability.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flag gated code behind scim-idempotency & scim-safe-deprovision. 2) Deploy to canary region, enable for internal tenants only. 3) Run reconciliation in dry-run for 48h for a pilot set of customers. 4) Enable corrective writes for pilot customers and monitor metrics for 72h. 5) Gradually enable for remaining tenants in weekly batches. 6) After 4 weeks, remove dry-run and monitor for regressions. Rollback: disable feature flag per-tenant and revert reconciliation corrective mode; tombstones are non-destructive so rollback is low-risk.
runbook:
- If reconciliation causes unexpected mass deletions: immediately disable corrective writes, enable dry-run, inspect reconciliation plan and audit log (scim.operation_id).
- If SCIM token store is slow: circuit-break to 429 for provisioning requests and surface clear message to admin console.
- If tombstone backlog grows unexpectedly: run targeted reconciliation in manual mode for affected tenant and contact SRE to scale workers.
- Contacts: SRE on-call, Security (Maya Chen), Product (Liam O'Connor).

comments: 2026-03-01 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after postmortem for partial SCIM failures impacting two enterprise customers. Goal is to eliminate repeated duplicate user creations and to avoid destructive deletes during intermediate failures.
2026-03-03 Rajat Singh: Spike completed for idempotency token design. Chose write-once token store with optimistic result_ref update to avoid double-apply. Documented in design doc.
2026-03-04 Maya Chen: Security review requested — flagged data retention for tokens; recommend 7 day TTL and encrypt token store at rest. Also request audit event schema be included in PR.

2026-03-06 Rajat Singh: Implemented tombstone columns and local unit tests. Running reconciliation dry-run against staging tenant data — found ~42 orphaned group memberships due to prior race condition.
2026-03-08 Priya Kapoor: Load test for token store at 1k req/s sustained — identified a hot key when using tenant-global lock; switched to sharded token buckets per tenant shard.
2026-03-09 Liam O'Connor: PM review — please add console UX copy for resync button and confirm admin RBAC permission required to trigger. Also coordinate release notes for customers.
2026-03-10 Rajat Singh: Feature flags created. Deploying to canary this afternoon. Security review scheduled for 2026-03-11.
2026-03-11 Maya Chen: Security review completed — approved with condition to include audit event for every reconciliation corrective write and KMS-encrypt token store.
